title: Bumps Myers, his mother, and playing with Buck Clayton's band
summary: He recalls how Bumps Myers's mother reminded him of his own and how this friendship led to work with Buck Clayton's band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You mentioned earlier about recording here in Los Angeles with musicians that you undoubtedly played a lot with around here, too. One of them was Bumps Myers.

Bumps Myers comes to mind particularly. Because one day I saw this lady going across the street, and she looked so much like my mother until I started to follow her. Then I found out it was Bumps Myers' mother, who we had become friends, so I was really...
I had just come to town, and Bumps had just come back from China with the Buck Clayton band -- Bumps and Eddie

Beal. So we became very good friends. As a matter of fact, Bumps and his mother took me in, and I was treated like a second son. Well, I'll be forever grateful to Bumps, and Eddie Beal, too, for the treatment they gave me. I was really taken right into the fold. So consequently, I got to play with Buck Clayton's band...

That was I guess 1937. Between 1937 and 1938, I think. I later played with... I guess I mentioned I had played with Lionel Hampton at the Cotton Club. Or did I? Anyhow, I did play with Lionel Hampton, too, so in case I said this before...
Oh, yes, I remember. You said it was at Frank Sebastian's Cotton Club.
